Button.summary: Triggers an action such as saving or continuing.
Button.when: Bind Command for application actions. Use click handlers for view-local behavior.
Button.pitfalls: A command that cannot execute can disable the button; inspect CanExecute before overriding IsEnabled.
Button.accessibility: Tab moves focus; Space and Enter activate according to focus and default-button behavior.

RepeatButton.when: Use for incremental adjustments rather than form submission.
RepeatButton.pitfalls: Avoid expensive synchronous work on every repeated invocation.
RepeatButton.accessibility: Keep an understandable name and visible focus.

ToggleButton.summary: Represents a selected action or mode.
ToggleButton.when: Use for persistent modes such as bold formatting.
ToggleButton.pitfalls: Bind checked state rather than inferring it from colors.
ToggleButton.accessibility: Expose checked state and visible focus.

CheckBox.summary: Edits an independent boolean or optional boolean choice.
CheckBox.when: Use when several independent choices can be selected.
CheckBox.pitfalls: Three-state values include indeterminate; do not treat null as false by accident.
CheckBox.accessibility: Provide a content label; Space toggles the focused option.

RadioButton.summary: Chooses one option in a group.
RadioButton.when: Use for a small visible set of mutually exclusive choices.
RadioButton.pitfalls: Give unrelated groups distinct group names.
RadioButton.accessibility: Verify keyboard navigation between options and label the group.

ToggleSwitch.summary: Turns an immediate setting on or off.
ToggleSwitch.when: Use for a binary setting with clear effects.
ToggleSwitch.pitfalls: Do not use a switch for a one-time action such as Save.
ToggleSwitch.accessibility: Label the setting independently of its on/off value.

Slider.summary: Adjusts a value within a numeric range.
Slider.when: Use for approximate adjustment such as volume.
Slider.pitfalls: Set meaningful bounds and increments; use numeric input for precision.
Slider.accessibility: Verify keyboard increments and an understandable name/value.

NumericUpDown.summary: Edits a numeric value with increment controls.
NumericUpDown.when: Use when a precise value and explicit increment matter.
NumericUpDown.pitfalls: Choose bounds, culture, formatting, and invalid-input behavior deliberately.
NumericUpDown.accessibility: Label the field and communicate errors with text.

ComboBox.summary: Chooses an item in a compact popup list.
ComboBox.when: Use when space is limited and options need not remain visible.
ComboBox.pitfalls: Preserve stable selected-item identities across updates.
ComboBox.accessibility: Test opening, navigating, choosing, and dismissing by keyboard.

TextBox.when: Configure wrapping and return acceptance for multiline content.
TextBox.pitfalls: Placeholder text is a hint, not a persistent label. Avoid resetting Text on each keystroke.
TextBox.accessibility: Provide a label, visible focus, and accessible validation messages.

TextBlock.when: Use for headings, labels, and short content.
TextBlock.pitfalls: A fixed-height parent can clip wrapped or scaled text.
TextBlock.accessibility: Allow text growth and keep foreground/background contrast readable.

SelectableTextBlock.summary: Displays text users can select and copy.
SelectableTextBlock.when: Use for identifiers, messages, and reference values.
SelectableTextBlock.pitfalls: Give the content enough room to select it.

Label.summary: Associates descriptive text with another control.
Label.when: Use for persistent field labels and access-key relationships.
Label.pitfalls: A visual text label does not automatically establish a target relationship.
Label.accessibility: Verify focus moves to the associated target.

RichTextBlock.when: Use for paragraphs and inlines beyond simple labels.
RichTextBlock.pitfalls: Test mixed scripts, long documents, and formatting boundaries.
RichTextBlock.accessibility: Verify reading behavior with the actual platform accessibility bridge.

RichEditBox.when: Use for document editing and formatting workflows.
RichEditBox.pitfalls: Document/selection APIs are richer than a plain TextBox Text value.
RichEditBox.accessibility: Test input methods, selection, keyboard editing, and screen readers.

Grid.summary: Arranges children into rows and columns.
Grid.when: Use for forms and regions dividing available space.
Grid.pitfalls: Star sizing needs a meaningful parent constraint.
Grid.accessibility: Preserve a sensible reading and tab order.

StackPanel.when: Use for a short vertical or horizontal flow.
StackPanel.pitfalls: An unconstrained stacking axis can defeat list virtualization.
StackPanel.accessibility: Keep child order meaningful when changing orientation.

WrapPanel.when: Use for tags, tiles, and tools that can flow.
WrapPanel.pitfalls: Wrapping alone does not provide item virtualization.
WrapPanel.accessibility: Check reading and keyboard order as line breaks change.

DockPanel.summary: Places children on edges around remaining content.
DockPanel.when: Use for a toolbar, status region, and central content.
DockPanel.pitfalls: Child order and last-child fill affect allocation.
DockPanel.accessibility: Keep edge regions usable in small windows.

Canvas.when: Use when coordinates are intrinsic, such as a diagram.
Canvas.pitfalls: Absolute positions do not adapt automatically to localization or text growth.
Canvas.accessibility: Provide a semantic keyboard model for interactive content.

UniformGrid.summary: Arranges children in equally sized cells.
UniformGrid.when: Use for regular grids with equal visual weight.
UniformGrid.pitfalls: Equal cell sizing differs from content-based Grid sizing.

Border.summary: Draws a frame, background, and padding around one child.
Border.when: Use for decorative or grouped content.
Border.pitfalls: A clickable Border does not supply Button semantics.
Border.accessibility: Do not add focus stops for purely decorative regions.

Viewbox.summary: Scales a child to fit available space.
Viewbox.when: Use for scalable artwork with a known logical size.
Viewbox.pitfalls: Scaling an entire form can make text and targets too small.
Viewbox.accessibility: Check readability and target size at every viewport.

ScrollViewer.when: Use when content overflows and does not own scrolling.
ScrollViewer.pitfalls: Nested scrolling can confuse input and undermine virtualization.
ScrollViewer.accessibility: Test keyboard scrolling and focus into off-screen content.

ContentControl.summary: Hosts a content value or data-template presentation.
ContentControl.when: Use for changing views or templated data.
ContentControl.pitfalls: Release subscriptions when discarded content leaves the view.
ContentControl.accessibility: Decide where focus belongs after content changes.

UserControl.summary: Packages a reusable composition of controls.
UserControl.when: Use for a reusable view; use a templated control for replaceable visuals.
UserControl.pitfalls: Avoid overwriting the inherited DataContext accidentally.
UserControl.accessibility: Keep the composition's reading and tab order meaningful.

ListBox.when: Use for a visible list of selectable records.
ListBox.pitfalls: Distinguish item-change from collection-change notifications and bound the viewport.
ListBox.accessibility: Test selection mode and arrow-key navigation.

ItemsControl.when: Use when repeated content needs no built-in selection model.
ItemsControl.pitfalls: Displaying items does not automatically establish selection.
ItemsControl.accessibility: Provide a keyboard model for interactive item content.

TreeView.pitfalls: Keep stable identities and define how expansion survives data changes.
TreeView.accessibility: Test expand/collapse and selection without a pointer.

TreeDataGrid.summary: Displays flat or hierarchical data in columns.
TreeDataGrid.when: Use when row hierarchy and tabular cells belong together.
TreeDataGrid.pitfalls: Use the grid's source and column contracts rather than ListBox templates.
TreeDataGrid.accessibility: Test cell navigation, selection, and expansion.

TabControl.when: Use for a small set of persistent destinations.
TabControl.pitfalls: Define whether changing tabs preserves state and retains expensive content.
TabControl.accessibility: Check keyboard tab selection and focus transfer.

NavigationView.when: Use for top-level destinations with a responsive navigation pane.
NavigationView.pitfalls: Selected navigation items are not automatically the application's route.
NavigationView.accessibility: Keep compact and expanded modes understandable.

Frame.pitfalls: Choose how page/view-model instances are cached and restored.
Frame.accessibility: Make the new context and focus destination clear.

SplitView.summary: Combines a collapsible pane with content.
SplitView.when: Use for responsive tools or side navigation.
SplitView.pitfalls: A pane is a layout mechanism, not a full route model.

Expander.summary: Reveals supporting content below a header.
Expander.pitfalls: Do not hide required error feedback in collapsed content.
Expander.accessibility: Communicate header purpose and expansion state.

Menu.when: Use for commands requiring predictable submenu behavior.
Menu.accessibility: Test keyboard traversal, Escape, and focus restoration.

ContextMenu.summary: Offers commands related to a target.
ContextMenu.when: Use as an alternative entry point for contextual actions.
ContextMenu.pitfalls: Do not make an essential action available only by right-click.
ContextMenu.accessibility: Test keyboard invocation and return focus.

ProgressBar.summary: Displays measurable progress or an indeterminate wait.
ProgressBar.when: Use a range for known progress and indeterminate state otherwise.
ProgressBar.pitfalls: Do not fabricate precise progress from an arbitrary timer.
ProgressBar.accessibility: Supply understandable text status as well as animation.

ToolTip.pitfalls: Do not put essential labels or validation only in a tooltip.
ToolTip.accessibility: Ensure keyboard users can obtain important information.

Calendar.summary: Selects dates within a calendar presentation.
Calendar.when: Use when surrounding dates help the choice.
Calendar.pitfalls: Distinguish a date-only value from a timestamp/time zone.
Calendar.accessibility: Test date navigation and localized presentation.

DatePicker.summary: Selects a date in a compact field.
DatePicker.when: Use for dates such as birthdays or deadlines.
DatePicker.pitfalls: Do not silently interpret a date-only value as UTC.
DatePicker.accessibility: Label the field and verify keyboard entry.

TimePicker.when: Use for clock times with an explicit domain meaning.
TimePicker.pitfalls: Define time-zone and daylight-saving handling in the model.

ColorPicker.when: Use when color selection is part of the task.
ColorPicker.pitfalls: Define alpha handling and serialization explicitly.
ColorPicker.accessibility: Provide textual color values and keyboard-operable controls.

NativeControlHost.when: Use for operating-system views or external native surfaces.
NativeControlHost.pitfalls: Clipping, transforms, focus, and lifetime differ by platform.
NativeControlHost.accessibility: Verify native accessibility and keyboard integration on real targets.

Window.when: Use for desktop windows and keep shared content in a reusable view.
Window.pitfalls: A desktop Window is not the browser or mobile main-view contract.
Window.accessibility: Test title, focus, system shortcuts, and accessible naming.
